ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Arts. L.561-2, L.561-45 to L.561-48; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 du 1er décembre 2016 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Décret n° 2018-284 du 18 avril 2018; Arrêté du 12 décembre 2018; Décret n° 2022-1259 du 22 septembre 2022 (FICOV – fichier des comptes et documents détenus par les établissements financiers); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); TRACFIN oversight; Reg. (EU) 2018/1673 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; sectoral note: trade-remedy defense consulting classified under APE 7490B requires no banking license, but client-facing representation before courts or the European Commission requires a practicing lawyer ('avocat') under Loi n° 71-1130 du 31 décembre 1971, Art. 54.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Birth certificate / official extract of civil status of each natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry office of the beneficial owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate intermediate stockholder (indirect UBO piercing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the intermediate entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney designating the French authorized representative to sign the RCS application and UBO declaration (formulaire M' – BO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or other competent authority in the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French-language public documents (traduction assermentée by a court-appointed translator)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required to carry the apostille itself; the underlying original must carry the apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FATF 40 Recommendations, EU consolidated sanctions list (Council Implementing Regulations of the European Council), UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (applicable because payment rails include SWIFT Wire and US-dollar denomination), and domestic French sanctions lists administered by TRACFIN and the Direction Générale du Trésor. Because the entity operates in anti-dumping and trade-remedy defense, additionally screen clients and counterparties against Regulation (EU) 2016/1036 (anti-dumping), Regulation (EU) 2016/1037 (anti-subsidy), and EU anti-circumvention proceedings; any party subject to an active EU trade-remedy measure imposes enhanced due diligence. PEP status of any beneficial owner or client triggers enhanced KYC under CMF Art. L.561-10 and ACPR guidelines; negative screening results must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years post-customer-relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (https://procedures.inpi.fr) with company and trademark search via data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe (RCS database)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Article 2 of the French Constitution mandates French as the language of the Republic; the chosen corporate name ('dénomination sociale') must be composed using the Latin alphabet with standard French diacritics to permit accurate registration in the RCS and publication in the BODACC. Foreign-language names and trademarks are permissible if transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by an optional registered French-language business name. Names likely to mislead the public as to the nature, nationality, or regulatory status of the entity are refused by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law provides no statutory company-name reservation separate from the incorporation filing; therefore, the 30-day window reflects the commonly observed professional holding period during which the applicant commits not to file competing names and may lock trade-name protection through an optional INPI trademark application. If the registry rejects the proposed name: (1) the applicant must receive a written, reasoned rejection notice from the Guichet Unique or the Greffe; (2) the applicant may immediately modify the name and re-file the incorporation dossier without payment of additional registry charges; (3) if the rejection is based on a substantive legal contest (e.g., prior identical registered name or protected trademark), the applicant may petition the président du tribunal judiciaire (procédure gracieuse) under Code de commerce Art. R.123-3 for judicial review of the registry decision within one month of the rejection; (4) alternatively, the applicant may file a claim in the commercial court for a declaratory ruling on distinctiveness; (5) in parallel, the applicant may file an opposition or invalidity action against a prior conflicting trademark before the INPI if the conflicting mark has been registered for more than five years and is non-distinctive or descriptive. Ordinary extension of the 30-day period is not available; a fresh name search and confirmation must be performed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable. An SAS must maintain a registered office ('siège social') in France. Use of a domiciliation company is permitted solely under Code de commerce Arts. L.123-11-2 and R.123-166 et seq., requiring the domiciliary to hold a prefectoral approval ('agrément'), maintain physical premises, and provide infrastructure enabling receipt of mail, professional contacts, and authorities. A pure mailbox-only virtual address without such physical substance is insufficient and is not accepted for a commercial trade-defense consultancy. The manager may alternatively domicile the company at his or her personal legal residence for a maximum of five years under Article L.123-11-1, after which the seat must be transferred to commercial premises or a licensed domiciliary.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5% annualized risk of unannounced physical verification by the Greffe, INPI, or tax authorities on grounds of commercial substance; risk increases to approximately 15% if the company's activities involve customs representation, import-export transactions, or active participation in EU anti-circumvention investigations requiring customs-site access, in which case DNRED (Direction Nationale du Renseignement et des Enquêtes Douanières) may conduct unannounced on-site inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Book II, Title II, Chapter VII: Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general incorporation provisions in Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing processed through the Guichet unique formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire de création d'entreprise (M0) accompanied by the executed Statuts constitutifs (articles of association).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: France imposes no legal minimum share capital for an SAS; the articles of association determine the amount. For incorporation, at least 50% of the aggregate nominal value of cash contributions must be paid up and held in a blocked bank account until registration, with the balance payable within five years. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at the time of issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the persons named in the subscribers' schedule hereby take up the issued share capital and make the corresponding contributions for incorporation of the Société par Actions Simplifiée. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be, and is hereby, established at the address inserted in the articles, effective immediately. RESOLVED, that the officer identified in the registration file is appointed as President and, if statutorily approved, Director General, with authority to represent the Company, open bank accounts, execute trade-defense consulting agreements, and complete all registration, licensing, and tax filings. RESOLVED, that counsel is authorized to make all declarations to the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, and competent licensing bodies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution, and notarization or authentication of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: No public filing window at this stage; executed before all shareholders or, where chosen, before a French notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft French-language articles of association compliant with Article L.227-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce; state share capital, share classes, corporate purpose, registered office, duration, and powers of the president. Have each shareholder sign the articles; if electronic signatures are used, use a qualified electronic signature service accepted by the registry. Optionally, execute the articles as an authentic deed before a notary to simplify real-property contributions or third-party validation.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Proof of physical address for each shareholder (utility bill dated within three months)
Draft articles of association describing capital, corporate purpose, and governance
Declaration of non-conviction or criminal record extract for each proposed legal representative
Company name availability search report from the INPI database
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the formal controller identifies a defect such as illegible signatures, incomplete capital allocation, or an incorrect corporate-purpose clause, re-execute the defective pages or the entire articles and re-sign. For notarized articles, request a corrected notarial instrument before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of share capital and blocking of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or notary holding the blocked funds account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the company in formation; transfer the subscribed cash capital from each shareholder; obtain a bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds) or notarial certificate. The funds remain frozen until the presentation of the RCS registration certificate or a written refusal; after registration, the bank releases the funds to the company. For in-kind contributions, prepare a valuation report by a statutory auditor if required.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of association
Identity documents of all subscribers
Subscriber bank reference details and proof of source of funds
Declaration of in-kind contributions and valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or due-diligence officer challenges the source of funds, provide the requested anti-money-laundering documents or adjust the contributing shareholder designation. If the bank refuses to issue the blocking certificate, correct the ownership or account denomination and obtain a new certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the formation notice in an approved legal announcement newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A juridical announcement newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) authorized in the territorial department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit a construction notice stating the corporate form, corporate name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and names of legal representatives. Publish the notice and obtain the attestation de parution from the newspaper for attachment to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Company project details from the articles of association
Share capital and legal representative data
Draft legal notice text in French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the newspaper requires corrections or refuses publication, amend the notice to comply with the publication standards and republish. If the published notice contradicts the articles, correct the articles if necessary and republish before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation application with the commercial registry through the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) on behalf of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0/application form and attach the certified document bundle: executed articles, capital blocking certificate, legal publication certificate, identity and address proofs of the president and officers, and declarations of non-conviction. Pay the statutory filing fee online. Upon admission, the registry issues the Kbis extract, which is definitive proof of legal existence and registration; the RCS number is allocated immediately by the INSEE directory.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 application form
Executed articles of association
Bank blocking certificate or notarial deed of capital deposit
Legal publication attestation de parution
Identity document of the president and each legal representative
Evidence of authority of the applicant signatory
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a query or regulatory request, respond within the prescribed period, modify the dossier electronically, and resubmit. If the defect is materially incurable, cancel the application and file a fresh dossier with corrected documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate governance and tax and employer onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for post-filing amendments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After delivery of the Kbis, convene and adopt the first board resolution, ratify the officers, and open the definitive professional bank account to receive the released capital. Complete the online business registration and tax formalities with DGFiP to obtain the taxpayer identification and any required VAT number; declare the actual commencement of activity. If employees will be hired, register the company as an employer with URSSAF and file the required workplace declarations.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
First board resolution or minutes of the corporate session
Articles of association
Company bank account details (RIB)
Officer appointment and remuneration records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority does not issue the VAT or taxpayer number within the statutory period, submit a formal request through the secured messaging area of impots.gouv.fr. If URSSAF does not issue the employer number, contact the business support center and provide a copy of the Kbis and registration proof.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Conseil National des Barreaux (regulatory bar council, applicable only where the activity includes French reserved legal services); otherwise no specific industrial licensing board is required for an office-based trade-defense consulting company.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: RCS registration and Kbis extract constitute the exhaustive operating licence for non-regulated consulting and trade-defense advisory services; where the activity includes reserved legal representation, the operating authorization is the professional bar admission certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based consulting activity is not listed in the annex to Article R.122-2 of the French Environment Code; no impact study or prior EIA notice is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or dust emission thresholds apply to an office-based trade-defense consultancy. All premises must nevertheless comply with general municipal waste collection obligations, building energy performance standards, and local noise regulations under the French Environmental Code (Articles L.541-1 et seq. for waste and Article R.1336-5 for noise).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire-safety conformity certificate from the local commission de sécurité for premises occupied by staff or receiving visitors. For new or renovated premises, obtain the building structural compliance certificate (attestation de solidité) and submit the workplace to the occupational health service. Prepare the mandatory workplace risk assessment document (document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels) and maintain employee medical and safety files.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr; corporate registrations and SIREN/SIRET allocation are effectuated through the Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Societe par Actions Simplifiee (SAS), the entity must complete the Guichet Unique electronic filing (M0 form) attaching the bylaws, registered office proof, and director identification; DGFiP then assigns a SIREN (9-digit), SIRET (14-digit), and an intra-Community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) for all EU taxable persons. A non-resident foreign enterprise without a French establishment that performs taxable services in France under articles 259, 259-A, and 283-2 of the French General Tax Code (CGI) must apply directly to the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises Etrangères (SIEE) for a French VAT number, appointing a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal accrédité) when not established in the EU. The client's Trade Remedy Defense Consulting scope requires a valid French VAT ID for any B2B or B2C supply invoiced in France, while the statutory professional license (legal representation) must be evidenced before the le gal practice authorization is granted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation, Territorial_Scope: The SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under article 206(1) CGI on all worldwide profits unless the permanent establishment exception applies; no tax-exempt zone relief applies to this ISIC 7490 service activity. The registered office and place of effective management in France render the SAS fully resident and within the full tax liability (territorialité mondiale with foreign tax credit mechanism).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under article 239 bis A CGI, a newly created SAS (less than 5 years old, fewer than 50 employees, turnover below EUR 10 million) may elect de transparence, i.e., to be taxed as a partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes), subjecting profits to income tax at shareholder level; this election is optional, must be filed with the local tax office within the first fiscal year, and lapses mandatorily after 5 years. France has enacted no separate 'check-the-box' hybrid classification; however, under article 210-0 A CGI, the SAS may elect for the tax integration regime (régime d'intégration fiscale) when it holds at least 95% of qualifying subsidiaries, and hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 1/2 (article 212 bis CGI, and the BEPS Action 2 transposition) disallow mismatched deduction outcomes unless the counterparty's treatment is aligned.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) under Directive 2006/112/EC and CGI articles 256 to 289 quater; no provincial or sub-national sales tax applies in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold applies to a large-business B2B consulting SAS; a French-established entity must register for VAT from its first taxable transaction regardless of turnover. For cross-border distance sales and electronically supplied services to French consumers by an EU vendor, the intra-Union distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; for a non-EU vendor supplying intangible/consulting digital services to a French non-taxable person, registration is mandatory from the first euro. The simplified small-business exemption (article 293 B CGI) applies only to French-established businesses with turnover not exceeding EUR 85,800 (goods) or EUR 37,500 (services), and is not available to the ISIC 7490 anti-dumping defense practice given the absence of low-turnover status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing will enter into force on 1 September 2026 (large taxpayers) and 1 September 2027 (SMEs), pursuant to the French e-invoicing reform (loi de finances 2022), requiring issuance and transmission through the public Portal Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Partenaire de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) using Factur-X/UBL/CII formats; e-invoicing data must be transmitted within 1 working day of invoice issuance. The reform does not impose real-time pre-clearance stamping as in Latin America; instead, automated e-reporting of transaction and status data is pushed to DGFiP, with invoices facing audit timestamps. For export transactions, the exporter must also file the electronic customs export declaration (DAU) via the DELTA/EBE system (Sonar) in real time before dispatch; the invoice itself stays a regular VAT document until the 2026 mandate applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under article 262 CGI, supplies of goods dispatched/transported outside the European Union are strictly exempt with credit (zero-rated) provided the exporter proves a 'véritable exportation' (genuine export); export evidence must be secured within 90 days of dispatch. Services ancillary to an export (freight, handling, trade-remedy legal defense directly connected to exported goods) qualify under article 262 CGI only if the service is directly linked to the physical export and invoiced to the exporter; B2B anti-dumping defense services provided to a foreign client normally fall outside French VAT (article 259-1 CGI), being taxable in the customer's country under the general B2B place-of-supply rule, not as zero-rated in France. For an SAS established in France, zero-rating applies to: (a) the supply itself when goods are shipped to a non-EU destination with transport documentation; (b) intra-Community supplies under article 262 ter CGI with the customer's valid EU VAT ID and recapitulative statement (EC Sales List); and (c) certain services directly linked to cross-border trade, subject to precise Evidenz documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Déclaration en Douane) validated via DELTA/Sonar with Movement Reference Number (MRN) and statement of exit (certificat d'expédition)
Bill of Lading (BCL) or Air Waybill (AWB) naming the French exporter as consignor/shipper with proof of physical departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice and pro forma, packing list, and underlying contract evidencing the anti-dumping defense service scope
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement showing receipt of payment from the non-EU customer within normal commercial terms
Proof of transport, i.e., CMR/transport contract or carrier report with route and final destination
For services: a written export declaration signed by the client (attestation de client) and documentary proof that the customer is a taxable person established outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French VAT law does not impose a 180-day statutory repatriation deadline per se; a 180-day reference period is retained in this dossier as the DGFiP documentary benchmark for export proceeds to be received in the exporter's French bank account, beyond which the fiscal administration may question the economic reality of the export and impose regular fines under article 1788 A CGI (5% penalty per quarter on unpaid VAT) and article 1728 CGI (10% late-payment penalty, escalating to 40% for deliberate misdeclaration under article 1729 CGI and 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses or abuse of right under articles 1729 b and L. 64 LPF). Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective clawback of the VAT exempted, interest (1.2% per month), 40%/80% penalties, and criminal exposure under the Douane Code (article 414) with up to 5 years' imprisonment and confiscation of goods; the Ministry of Economy may also ban the exporter from export operations. For trade-remedy defense consulting, DGFiP rigorously scrutinizes that the service is physically rendered from France to a non-EU beneficiary and not resold or deemed rendered to a French entity under the mid-distance rules of article 259-1 CGI.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting as the National Central Bank; supervised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking compliance, with FX and Balance of Payments surveillance coordinated with the European Central Bank and the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a full convertibility regime for both current and capital account transactions within the EU/EEA under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Non-EU/EEA cross-border flows are unrestricted but are subject to statistical Balance of Payments (BOP) declarations to the Banque de France, with an overriding 150,000 EUR threshold for direct investment declarations. Capital injections and profit remittances are freely convertible from EUR to any foreign currency, provided that the underlying funds are of documented legitimate origin. Dividend and profit distributions are freely remittable to non-resident shareholders after satisfaction of French corporate tax and withholding tax rules, including participation-exemption relief under Article 145 of the French General Tax Code and protection under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. As a euro-area resident under the euro single currency, a French SAS may retain export revenues in EUR or any foreign currency, and there is no obligation to liquidate foreign-currency balances into EUR. Day-to-day receipts from trade-defense services are recorded via normal invoicing, and any exceptionally large cross-border receipts are reported by the receiving bank under the Banque de France BOP reporting regime for statistical monitoring only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / EUR Operational Current Account
Operational Current Account / Dedicated Client-Funds Sub-Account
Operational Current Account / Liquidity Deposit Account
Operational Current Account / Regulated Collateral Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. French-authorized electronic money institutions (EMIs) under the PSD2 regime are permissible for collecting trade-defense consultancy fees in EUR and, where passported, in EU currencies; however, EMIs are prohibited from granting commercial credit or providing corporate treasury concentration services and cannot serve as the sole capital-injection rail. Non-EU/EEA digital EMIs are generally not viable because French laws require either a full credit institution license or a properly passported EMI registration with the ACPR, leading to practical account-opening refusals for a foreign-licensed EMI without a French branch.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is strongly required in practice for a non-resident-owned SAS. Under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L.561-5 et seq.) and ACPR AML/CFT obligations, corporate onboarding mandates an interview with the beneficial owners and directors. Remote onboarding via regulated video-identification (e.g., official DIM process for a French e-ID card) is allowed only for individual clients; for a corporate client acting in the anti-dumping defense sector, BNP Paribas and Société Générale consistently require an in-person meeting with at least one director in France or, exceptionally, with a formally appointed resident corporate officer/managing agent holding a power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership and opaque UBO structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory UBO declaration filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) demonstrating the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) disclosure; certified passport, proof of residence, corporate bylaws certified in the country of residence; apostilled or legalized corporate extract with chain-of-title evidence and confirmation of absence of shell-company indicia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse- or high-risk counterparty exposure arising from cross-border trade-defense clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client engagement letters, commercial contracts, detailed invoices describing the exact scope of anti-dumping filing defense and compliance advice; a risk-based client classification memorandum confirming no dealings with sanctioned entities; additional source-of-wealth documentation from clients with exposure to historically sensitive jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed-purpose or unusually large inbound wire flows linked to intercompany services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy setting out purpose codes; board-approved engagement schedule; signed attestation that the business scope (ISIC 7490 – anti-dumping defense consulting) does not involve prohibited customs circumvention; full source-of-funds evidence, including bank statements confirming client payments and, where relevant, underlying legal-defense fee memos.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections by non-resident shareholders must be routed through the SWIFT network using MT103 (customer transfer) or MT202 (financial institution transfer), with the OECD/unified European BOP classification code IRED (investment in equity capital of a French resident enterprise) or the bank-specific equivalent. The initiating bank must obtain the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of the French SAS and pass a beneficiary-verification directive. Settlement in EUR can occur via the Banque de France T2/Target2 euro system; for cross-currency injections (e.g., USD/EUR), banks execute a spot FX conversion at client's cost with confirmation of commercial-origin purpose. Where the investor is domiciled outside the EU/EEA, the French receiving bank will require a declaration to the DG Trésor for statistical/direct-investment monitoring if the cumulative injection exceeds the applicable threshold (generally 150,000 EUR) and will ensure the funds are recorded on the BOP direct-investment surveillant statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-defense consulting disbursements (expert review fees, customs-lawyer retainers, local-counsel advances, translator costs) are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for non-EU counterparties and via the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA Credit Transfer scheme for EU/EEA beneficiaries. For high-value disbursements linked to litigation, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) is generally not used because the services are non-goods-based; instead, escrowed disbursement undertakings and unconditional bank-guarantee payments are deployed. All outbound wires must carry the applicable purpose code, and amounts above 10,000 EUR are subject to automatic ACPR AML screening; execution time is T+0 for SEPA and T+1 to T+3 for non-SEPA USD/EUR wires.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) for assured trade-defense fee receipts denominated in non-EUR currencies
FX swaps (short-term simultaneous spot/forward combinations) for overnight and week-end liquidity smoothing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly documented for emerging-market counterparties where deliverability is unavailable and where no speculative intent is demonstrated
Vanilla over-the-counter FX options (call and put) with a clear hedging rationale, subject to EMIR clearing thresholds and ACPR margining rules
Cross-currency swaps solely for matched-inflow/outflow alignment when the SAS receives foreign-currency fee prepayments and incurs non-EUR disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the date of the Ordinary General Meeting (AGM held within 6 months after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 5,000 EUR and potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to 5,000 EUR and risk of company dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if turnover exceeds 50 million EUR, total assets exceed 43 million EUR, or average number of employees exceeds 500
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) or IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update and filing of beneficial ownership information to the RCS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.00% standard corporate income tax rate for fiscal years closing on or after 1 January 2022 (art. 219 CGI). A reduced 15.00% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for small enterprises meeting all statutory conditions (taxable turnover below EUR 10,000,000; fully paid-up share capital below EUR 7,500,000; at least 75% held by individuals or qualifying companies). A 3.3% social surcharge on corporate income tax applies to companies with turnover above EUR 7,630,000, unless repealed by the applicable annual Finance Act.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research tax credit (CIR): 30% of eligible research expenditures up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above (art. 244 quater B CGI). Innovation tax credit (CII): 20% of eligible innovation expenses capped at EUR 400,000 (art. 244 quater B bis CGI). Preferential IP regime: 10% effective rate on net qualifying patent and equivalent intangible royalties (art. 238 CGI). No notional interest deduction for equity. For an anti-dumping and trade-defense consulting SAS, CIR/CII generally have limited relevance absent distinct research or prototype activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited duration (report en avant is indefinite under art. 209 I CGI), subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit in excess of EUR 1,000,000. Carry-back (report en arrière) is abolished for fiscal periods ending on or after 31 December 2023.
